mn_palisade_head.blurb:
Palisade Head is a tall rhyolite headland rising straight out of Lake Superior on Minnesota's North Shore, inside Tettegouche State Park. Its steep, crack-seamed faces make it the state's best-known trad destination, with lines from 5.6 up through the 5.12s and a handful of 5.13 and harder test pieces.

Most of the climbing is traditional crack and face work, and many parties top-rope off fixed anchors above the cliff; a few sport, aid and winter ice lines round out the mix. The setting is dramatic and exposed, so it suits climbers comfortable placing gear and rappelling or scrambling to reach the base.

co_duncan_s_ridge.blurb:
Duncan's Ridge is a short hogback of sandstone on the west side of Horsetooth Reservoir near Fort Collins. Its trad lines run from 5.4 to 5.11, most of them easy to top-rope from above, and there is a scattering of tall boulder problems as well.

Because the walk is brief and the routes are approachable, it suits beginners, instructors and groups, as well as boulderers looking for highballs. The rock faces the reservoir in full sun, so summer afternoons run hot and early or late sessions are more comfortable.

co_penitente_inner_canyon.blurb:
The Inner Canyon is the deeper section of Penitente Canyon, a volcanic-walled sport-climbing venue in the San Luis Valley near La Garita. The routes are bolted and span a very wide range, from beginner 5.3 climbs up to 5.14, with the bulk between 5.10 and 5.12, so there is something for most parties.

The canyon is known for pocketed, textured walls and slabs, and its short, flat trails make it easy to hop between routes in a day. Boulders around the canyon floor add bouldering for rest days.
co_penitente_inner_canyon.approach: Short, mostly flat trails lead from the canyon parking up the canyon floor to the walls; the slab routes near the back of the main canyon are a handy landmark for the inner walls.

wv_long_point.blurb:
Long Point is a cliff on the shore of Summersville Lake in the Gauley River area, with a mix of quality trad lines and strong sport routes from 5.6 to 5.13, the bulk at 5.10 to 5.12 on both bolts and gear.

The base is only walkable when the reservoir is drawn down, so it is a fall and winter destination. It catches morning sun until around midday, which makes cold-season days pleasant, and it suits climbers who want less-crowded rock near the more popular lake cliffs.

ut_green_adjective_gully.blurb:
A gully tucked into the lower part of Little Cottonwood Canyon beside the Gate Buttress, in the Wasatch. It holds a dense mix of short trad lines, some sport routes, toprope problems, a little aid, and boulder problems on the blocks in and around the gully.

Most of the roped climbing is single pitch, around a hundred feet, with crack and corner lines from 5.4 up to the 5.13s and most at 5.11 and 5.12, plus boulder problems from V2 to V11. Its low elevation and short walk from the road make it a handy quick-hit spot for climbers based in Salt Lake City.

co_contest_wall.blurb:
The Contest Wall is the first-sun side of Sand Gulch at Shelf Road, near Cañon City, an easy walk from the campground there. Its routes are bolted face climbs on pocketed limestone, mostly one pitch of fifty to a hundred feet.

Grades run from 5.7 through the low 5.12s, with most at 5.10 and 5.11, and the stock of moderate lines makes it popular with newer sport climbers and groups. A few trad lines, toprope setups and boulder problems round out the wall, and it is a good choice on cool days when the morning sun is welcome.

co_lincoln_lake.blurb:
A quiet zone of alpine granite bouldering south of the main road on Mt. Blue Sky, formerly Mount Evans, with the blocks sitting above 10,000 feet. The rock is rough and featured with plenty of incut edges, and the problems are generally short, twenty to thirty feet, including traverses and highballs; grades run from V0 to V14 with the bulk from V7 to V10.

Reaching these boulders takes a strenuous hike, which keeps crowds low compared with the busier zones nearby. Most of the area lies inside wilderness, so climbers carry their pads in and out and keep chalk use light. The season is short, and it suits fit boulderers happy to trade a long approach for solitude.

ct_main_cliff.blurb:
The Main Cliff is the centrepiece of Ragged Mountain on the Southington and Berlin line, on the Metacomet Ridge: a west-facing traprock wall with routes up to about a hundred feet, climbed since the 1930s, which gives it a strong traditional feel and a long list of classics.

Routes run from 5.3 to 5.12, most between 5.8 and 5.10, with a mix of slabs, cracks and corners. Many are traditional leads that call for solid skills; others are easier and set up for toprope, with some bouldering below. It draws a steady crowd from across central Connecticut and southern New England.
ct_main_cliff.approach: Walk in along the Blue Trail (the New England Scenic Trail) from the trailhead parking, then follow the undercliff trail along the base to reach the routes.
